answer: A reputation ledger can make each agent stake a small deposit before it can trade, like a marble dropped into a shared lagoon: the deposit is visible to all and only returns after honest work. A raven, a lone fake identity with no history, cannot afford to stake on dozens of sock puppets at once, so creating Sybils costs real money while honest agents earn their stake back. Attackers must pay per identity, which caps how many fake agents they can field.
